sources.entry: Manyfold - Digital asset manager for 3d print files; STL, OBJ, 3MF and more. (Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Manyfold is a self-hosted, open source web application for managing a collection of 3D models, focused on 3D printing.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Manyfold as a self-hosted web app for organizing 3D model collections, particularly for 3D printing. It is a server-side Ruby on Rails app using plain HTTP requests, with a Sidekiq background job runner for asynchronous tasks. The client-side 3D rendering uses THREE.js (via TypeScript), and server-side 3D code uses Mittsu, a Ruby port of THREE.js. The README says PostgreSQL is used in production and SQLite in development. Development setup covers a devcontainer, Rubocop/StandardRB and ERB/TypeScript linters, RSpec and Guard test workflows, and I18n translation via Translation.io. The README mentions assimp for model file analysis and ImageMagick for thumbnails. Full user and admin documentation is on the project website, not in the README.
use_cases: Organizing a library of 3D printing models
Contributing to a Ruby on Rails open source project
how_to_run: Clone the repository and install the prerequisites listed in the README: Ruby 3.4, Bundler 2.6+, Node.js, Yarn 3.8+, Foreman, libarchive, ImageMagick, ngrok and assimp
Run `bin/dev` from the repository root to set up the database, run migrations, install dependencies and start the app
Optionally create `.env.development.local` from `env.example` to configure optional features
Alternatively, open the repo in VS Code and use the devcontainer configuration
To build a Docker image, run `docker build -f docker/default.dockerfile .` in the repository root
notable: Built on Ruby on Rails with server-side rendering over plain HTTP requests, without XHR or WebSockets
Client-side 3D viewing with THREE.js and server-side 3D model analysis with Mittsu
Multi-platform Docker image built by Depot, with a devcontainer for VS Code development
Translations managed through Translation.io and client-side i18n via i18n-js
Supports ActivityPub federation, with an ngrok tunnel setup for development
caveats: Production deployment needs PostgreSQL; the README says SQLite is used only in development
Development setup needs several external tools (Ruby 3.4, Node.js, ImageMagick, assimp, libarchive, ngrok, Foreman)
The README says Windows users should clone into WSL to avoid slow file access
